transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

Some programmes, such as cool air, refresh, delicates or a low-heat option, dry with little or no heat. Was a cool-air or low-heat programme set (and have you changed it), or was it a normal heat programme?
No, it's a normal heat programme, and it's cold on both high and low heat settings. Dial and lights all work as normal.

Thanks for letting us know about the lack of heat on that normal programme. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. A blocked lint filter stops airflow, causing many dryers to cut the heat to prevent overheating. Clean the fluff filter located in the door opening; note that heat-pump models often have a second one at the bottom too. You can refer to the picture shown below for guidance on where to find these filters. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the lint filter is" — The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.]
The lint filter was fairly full, I've cleaned it now. Still no heat though, do I need to check anything else before I order a part?

Thanks for letting us know about the issue. Before we proceed, please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Then check the vent hose at the back of the machine. It should be short, without kinks or squashed sections, and clear of fluff all the way to the outside vent. Was it kinked, squashed or blocked (and is it sorted), or was it already clear?
The vent hose goes out a window and had a sag full of fluff. I've cleaned it out and airflow at the end is decent now, but it's still cold after running 20 min.

[Heading: Heater / thermal cut-out / thermostat]
Thank you for confirming the vent is clear and that the dryer remains cold despite using a normal heat programme with a clean lint filter. Since airflow is unobstructed but there is still no heat, the issue likely lies with the heater element, its thermal cut-out or the thermostat. These components require testing by an appliance engineer, as a tripped cut-out usually indicates an underlying reason. I am not recommending any specific parts for you to replace at this stage.
